item.title: UK Cultural Organisations Call on Andy Burnham to Address EU Touring Issues
item.dc:creator: Christian Eede
item.description:
Artists have faced visa issues, increased transportation costs and more since the UK's exit from the European Union

Over 300 live music and cultural organisations have signed an open letter calling on Prime Minister Andy Burnham to address continued issues that UK artists face when touring countries in the European Union (EU).

Artists, performers and other cultural figures have faced "major barriers" to touring in the area since the UK left the EU in January 2020, according to the letter. These include issues surrounding visas, and increased costs in transporting instruments and other equipment, as well as various other logistical problems.

The letter was put together and submitted to Burnham by the Cultural Exchange Coalition (CEC), a coalition that represents organisations such as UK...

item.title: The Strange World of… Suzanne Ciani
item.dc:creator: John Doran
item.description:
In her eightieth year, during her first ever trip to Scotland to close Sonica festival in Glasgow, electronic music pioneer Suzanne Ciani looks back on her career with Claire Sawers. Main portrait: Dan Wilton

From her early days studying classical composition, to her game-changing friendship with the electronic instrument designer Don Buchla, Suzanne Ciani was always interested in world building. Her ability to create vast, echoing dreamscapes or equally impactful sonic miniatures has gained her huge respect and a broad, multi-generational fanbase; one that didn’t exist at the outset, as the technologies she used were initially only known to a handful. 

Ciani persevered with her progressive approach through the 1970s and 80s, strategically funding her creative projects with lucrative corporate work, which...

item.title: Tara Cunningham – Warm Ground
item.dc:creator: Robert Barry
item.description:
Tara Cunningham

Warm Ground

Tara Cunningham’s latest mini-LP of small wonders proves a perfect counterpoint to our outsized era, says Bernie Brooks

Warm Ground by Tara Cunningham

We’re living through an era of apocalyptic sizing, of catastrophic scale. El Niño, high temperatures, glacier melt, funding cuts, deregulation, wealth inequality, the AI bubble, etc. Even the good stuff is epochal. In the US, the Democrat win a week or so ago was Texas-sized. If all this XXXL news were as peachy as that, that’d be one thing, but it isn’t. It mostly isn’t. And that’s more than mostly exhausting.

So, imagine my delight when the new Tara Cunningham record, Warm Ground, described in the presser as a mini-LP of miniatures, appeared – as if by providence...

item.title: Brokeback Return with First Album in Over 10 Years
item.dc:creator: Christian Eede
item.description:
Thrill Jockey will release Colder, Milder in February

Photo by John Sturdy

Brokeback, the band led by Tortoise's Douglas McCombs, have announced their first album in over a decade.

Spanning eight tracks, Colder, Milder sees the quartet refine their post-surf rock sound, prioritising simplicity and restraint, according to a press release. It's led by the title track, which you can listen to below.

In a statement about the lead cut, McCombs said: "This song was built around the three-note figure in the verses, simple. The guitar harmonies that start the song and recur halfway through were imagined as Everly Brothers vocal harmonies, but didn’t really end up sounding like that."

Thrill Jockey will release Colder, Milder on 26 February 2027.

item.title: Spydergum – Spydergum
item.dc:creator: Robert Barry
item.description:
Spydergum

Spydergum

Featuring Concepción Huerta and Luka Aron among others, this large improvising ensemble contains multitudes

Spydergum by Spydergum

It is sticky and it penetrates the skin. That tingling feeling is tortuously triggering. Attentive listening is what is calling for Spydergum. This is the way the expansive electroacoustic ensemble mark the year with their most anticipated eponymous debut release. Their first record, a fully improvised body of work, is a testimony to the fact that to co-create means to begin to listen deep.

Spydergum is an ecosystem of simultaneously communicating sonic bodies, encompassing an ever-morphing sticky web of diverse voices and instruments. The group is currently constituted by twenty-plus well-established international improvisers, producers and songwriters. Born out of informal gatherings during a one-week residency at...

item.title: Paint it Black: Saints in The Wethouse by Blackhaine
item.dc:creator: Robert Barry
item.description:
The "debut album" by the Preston-born musician, rapper and choreographer establishes Blackhaine as one of the most confident voices in the new Northern Gothic scene developing around Yorkshire and Lancashire

Credit: Archie Finch

In the film, The King (2019), we see a stubborn Dauphin of France attempting to end the Battle of Agincourt through a duel with King Henry. Heavy rainfall has left the ground entirely sodden, and before a single blow is dealt, the Dauphin is slipping and sliding around the squelchy ground, falling over and over again. He is tragically defenceless and vulnerable as he performs an unchoreographed, increasingly desperate dance of misery before being swiftly slaughtered and left dead in the mud.

item.title: Tehran Contemporary Sounds Festival Takes Place in Berlin
item.dc:creator: Christian Eede
item.description:
The latest edition of the event takes in performances from Abdullah Miniawy, Gnäw and more

Abdullah Miniawy

Tehran Contemporary Sounds Festival is taking place in Berlin this week.

Stretching out across six days, the seventh edition of the event brings together live performances, film screenings, talks and audiovisual presentations. The programming, which largely celebrates work by the Iranian diaspora, is spread across Berlin's Silent Green Kulturquartier venue, while film screenings are taking place at Moviemento Kino.

The bulk of the music programming appears across this week, from 13 to 15 November. It will feature performances from Abdullah Miniawy, Gnäw, Ava Rasti and the duo Tehran, among others. Check out the full schedule of events here.

item.title: Armand Hammer Surprise Release New Album, ‘Snakes & Ladders’
item.dc:creator: Christian Eede
item.description:
It features guest appearances from DJ Haram and $ilkmoney

Armand Hammer, the duo of billy woods and ELUCID, have released a surprise new album, Snakes & Ladders.

Featuring 16 tracks, it follows on from last year's Mercy LP, and features guest appearances from DJ Haram and $ilkmoney. There is also production from clipping., and frequent collaborators such as Kenny Segal, Preservation, Child Actor and Sebb Bash.

The album was written and recorded by Armand Hammer and their collaborators in the winter of 2025 into 2026. Its release comes as the duo round off their tour of North America this week, with the final show scheduled for Sunday (15 November) at New York's Music Hall of Williamsburg.

item.title: Coachella Reveals 2027 Lineup
item.dc:creator: Christian Eede
item.description:
Madonna, SZA and Giorgio Moroder are among the artists playing next year's festival in California

Coachella has revealed its full 2027 lineup.

The California festival will be headlined by SZA, Dua Lipa and Tame Impala, while Madonna is also listed to play a special set in the Sahara dance music tent, following a 2006 appearance she did there after putting out her album Confessions On A Dance Floor. On the verge of her debut solo album, Radie Peat of Lankum and ØXN presents 13 records that have held sway over her life and work, from Nico to Beak >

Radie Peat is rightly known as a generational talent in traditional folk music. Coil

Assembled from the discarded off-cuts from Horse Rotorvator and the group's unused Hellraiser score, Coil's third album proves far more than the sum of its parts

Gold Is The Metal (With The Broadest Shoulders) by Coil

Alchemy. The protoscientific transmutation of base materials into “noble metals” such as gold is a well documented theory more closely aligned with philosophical and spiritual traditions than tangible science. In Alejandro Jodorowsky’s cult work of psychedelic cinema, The Holy Mountain, the protagonist defecates in a bell jar and inhales the rotting fumes in a bid to turn himself into gold.

item.dc:creator: John Doran

Wipers would have been huge if they hadn't asked so many questions. John Calvert writes about an essential punk album from 45 years ago

On Portland Punk Live At The Earth 10-29-79, a live-on-the-night document of local bands released warts'n'all by Wipers' Greg Sage on his own label, Trap, Sage can be heard introducing his band's 'Same Old Thing'. The latest from Mari Rubio builds complex scaffolding from the simplest of motifs

valley and structure by more eaze

Over the last few years, I’ve seen More Eaze (aka Mari Rubio) twice. At Rewire in 2022, she performed as -----__, a digital, detail-laden project created in collaboration with Seth Graham. item.dc:creator: Patrick Clarke
item.description:
Celebrating its 20th year, with a lineup focussed on bypassing arbitrary boundaries, Utrecht's flagship experimental festival forces even the most eclectic listener to go beyond, says Patrick Clarke

Bethlehem's Lawrence Sammour, photo by Maarten Mooijman

We start Le Guess Who? 2026 with Tortoise, who draw an enormous crowd in the cavernous Ronda space within Utrecht’s TivoliVredenburg complex. They offer a masterful display of how the subtlest shifts can produce the biggest effects, a tiny buzz of synth blooming slowly into something majestic and warm; a small nudge of bass snowballing until it’s an avalanche. item.title: Claire Cronin – The Bruise
item.dc:creator: Robert Barry
item.description:
Claire Cronin

The Bruise

The folk horror Sandy Denny sees the horror of it all all too clearly

The Bruise by Claire Cronin

“Female singer songwriter” is a designation packed full of dated assumptions male singer songwriters have not had to contend with since the 60s. The category not only fails to illuminate, but flattens all difference, forcing artists who have very little in common to seem more similar than they are.

Claire Cronin is too touched by the uncanny to succumb to any such kookiness-at-all-costs shoehorning. item.dc:creator: Christian Eede
item.description:
Its release marks their signing to Indiana label Joyful Noise, and the founding of their own imprint, Well-Tempered Zealot

Dirty Projectors have released a new song, called 'Jumbotron'.

It comes amid a flurry of activity from the project, which is led by David Longstreth. They've newly signed to Indiana label Joyful Noise, and launched their own imprint, Well-Tempered Zealot.

Speaking about 'Jumbotron', Longstreth said: "I was thinking about the big screen and the small screen. The big tent and the kind of tent you can make in the living room with a couple couch cushions and a blanket or two. Life and entertainment; attention and volume; focus and detail; quality and value. Khudgarzi by Sheherazaad

“There’s this fantastical, romanticised thing of being in grief and being dark and depressed, and then doing your best work,” American composer and theatre artist Sheherazaad tells me. A mere two months ago, she lost her grandmother, who was herself a music producer and, in many ways, the only other woman she knew who shared her intense, sometimes isolating relationship with music.

Ana Lua Caiano

Devagar Que A Vida É Curta

Portuguese singer-producer draws on Zeca Afonso and modern digital production techniques to produce a thrilling call to action

Devagar Que A Vida É Curta by Ana Lua Caiano

Devagar Que A Vida É Curta translates loosely as ‘Go slowly as life is short’. The title track does anything but go slowly, a frantic 43 seconds where Ana Lua Caiano’s assertive, multitracked vocals get in as much information as possible before the proverbial window closes. In Portuguese, she gasps: “Life is beautiful, beautiful, beautiful / Oh life, run slowly… Death is near, move fast…”

item.title: English Folk Dance and Song Society Changes Name
item.dc:creator: Patrick Clarke
item.description:
It marks a major shift as the organisation approaches its centenary

Cecil Sharp House

The English Folk Dance and Song Society (EFDSS) has formally changed its trading name to Folk England, a decision it says aligns with a mission to "make folk music, song, and dance inclusive for all."

The organisation was founded in 1932 following the merger of the Folk-Song Society and the English Folk Dance Society. The decision to change its name now represents one of the biggest changes in the organisation's history.

Katy Spicer, Chief Executive & Artistic Director of Folk England, said of the decision: “For some years we have recognised that the breadth and ambition of the organisation’s work has far outgrown the confined and outdated previous name and...

item.title: 45 Years On: OMD’s Architecture & Morality Remembered
item.dc:creator: John Doran
item.description:
Orchestral Manoeuvres In The Dark released one of the Quietus' favourite albums in 1981. John Doran reflects on the warmth of Architecture & Morality and talks to Andy McCluskey

A lazy but widespread criticism of the English synth pop scene of the early 80s was that it was soulless or lacking in human warmth. While there certainly were acts who came across as detached or alienated (Cabaret Voltaire, The Normal, John Foxx) if anything, the opposite was generally true. There is an almost baroque level of (exquisitely judged) romantic melodrama to Soft Cell's 'Say Hello Wave Goodbye'; despite Gary Numan's dead-eyed automaton image, Tubeway Army's 'Are "Friends" Electric?' is quite clearly a very fragile and keenly felt song about heartbreak; and...

Why Listen to Animals? asks Francis Gooding after immersing himself in some questionable musique concrète

Symphony Natura by Henning Christiansen and Lorenzo Mammi

"The zoo", wrote John Berger in a 1977 essay called 'Why Look At Animals?', "cannot but disappoint". The purpose of the visit is to see the animals, to look at them, but the animals always avoid being seen: they are bunched up at the edge of their enclosures, they are lethargic, they are hidden in their sleeping quarters, they are indifferent to the visitor. Berger was writing about the scopic regime of the zoological garden: it is a place where one goes to look at animals, and no matter the real or imagined conservation functions of the modern zoo,...

World's End is out in February

Photo by Jimmy Mould

Tim Reaper will release his debut solo album, World's End, via Hyperdub early next year.

Featuring 11 tracks, the LP follows the jungle producer's previous collaborative album with Kloke, In Full Effect, which Hyperdub put out in 2024. In recent years, he's continued to put out EPs at a steady rate via labels such as FABRICLIVE, Rinse, Astrophonica and his own Future Retro London.

World's End naturally explores various shades of jungle, as well as footwork, drill and gqom.
